description:
I go deep on the Hermes desktop plugin SDK — mapping every place a plugin can live, then building some that really push it.

▶️ Want more On-Chain AI Garage? Hit Join to become a member. Team Garage gets early access to new videos; Team Garage Live adds a weekly livestream where you can ask questions, talk AI, and watch me build live: https://www.youtube.com/@TonbisAIGarage/join

🧠 Run agents? Give them a knowledge base. Agent Wikis has free, curated LLM wikis on a ton of AI topics — plus a Pro tier ($9.99/mo) for super-sized wikis with way more depth: https://agentwikis.com/

Sign up for my FREE weekly newsletter, where I spill my unfiltered thoughts on the latest AI news, cool research, and projects I'm building: https://www.onchainaigarage.com/

A follow-up to my Hermes desktop plugin intro, this one is a proper deep dive: I build a "Placement Playground" plugin that cycles through all 25 spots a plugin can live — panes, workspace, status bar, title bar, composer, popovers — so you can see how form should follow function. I break down where a plugin's power comes from (Hermes state, a backend, browser media) and, just as importantly, what it flat-out can't do. Then I push the SDK with three real builds: a read-only Hyperliquid trading terminal, a Spotify controller, and an SNES emulator I can play while my agent works.

Resources:
🔗 Hermes Agent: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

10:31 - Where a plugin's power comes from — and its limits
13:00 - Building a trading terminal (Hyperliquid)
15:51 - A Spotify controller plugin
17:43 - An SNES emulator plugin
